evidenceInspected.disclosure: Variant definitions and existing editorial captions were visible during inspection. Judgment is independent but this was not a blinded review. Full batch statistics and full-match clips were not evaluated.

observations.facts: Blue has a more legible outlined preparation ring in B at 8.6/8.9; by 9.0 a projectile is visible in both. At 9.3 red has 80 HP in both and B adds a white mark on red. Logs put blue release at 8.967 and damage at 9.25.
observations.interpretation: B makes a useful distinction between getting a shot ready and confirming contact. The visible shot already communicates travel in A; the improvement is additional phase information, not a wholly new readable attack.

observations.facts: B shows red preparing near blue at 9.6, then a small release cue at 9.7 without a white damage mark; blue remains 34 HP. Later frames show blue at 12 HP and then dead with a white mark at the finishing position in B. Logs distinguish red release without damage at 9.633 from damaging melee at 11.433 and 12.217.
observations.interpretation: The missed swing is the strongest useful test: an action occurred without a successful hit. B helps avoid equating every effect with success. But even with B, the stills do not explain why that swing missed or prove that I would read the pressure reversal at normal playback speed.

observations.facts: Both panels retain red/green contact, yellow projectiles, and blue firing. B puts a white mark near green after green dies and on red after yellow damage; later small marks appear around the red/yellow contact. At 7.3 the remote ice impact has no matching hit mark. Logs record green dying at 6.983, empty ice at 7.233 and yellow damage to red at 7.567/7.600.
observations.interpretation: B makes the recipient of damage easier to locate while preserving the intersecting engagement. It does not independently identify the attacker: yellow projectiles and red melee still need to be followed. A white cross should be described as damage happened here, never as proof of who had initiative or why a dodge failed.

observations.facts: B outlines green and yellow preparation at 0.5 and shows small release accents around the rapid-fire sequence. By 1.1 red has a prominent white mark; green later loses HP while the right-hand projectile chain continues. At 2.4 the ice has landed away from fighters without a white impact cross there. Logs record multiple spread hits on red within 0.983–1.017, melee damage to green at 1.367/2.167, and zero-hit ice at 2.317.
observations.interpretation: This contrary case shows the information is compact enough that bodies/projectiles remain visible in these samples. Still, the floor has charge rings, a large ice warning, tiny release rings and projectile trails together. Their priority is weak at this scale; I can understand damage more readily than which threat deserves my next look. Multiple simultaneous damage crosses should not be counted visually as distinct causally traced attacks.

rankedConcerns.concern: Initiative remains difficult to read when multiple fighters act. Confirming a victim is easier than seeing who controls space or what escape is available.
rankedConcerns.severity: Material limit on the claim; not a blocker to comparing these alternatives.

rankedConcerns.concern: Preparation and release cues are small at the supplied two-panel scale; the ring outlines are clearer than their exact progression or directional detail.
rankedConcerns.severity: Needs owner judgment in motion; do not claim anticipation solved.

rankedConcerns.concern: Hit confirmation establishes actual damage but not attacker/projectile lineage or the reason an attack missed. Empty explosions and absent hit marks require careful wording.

tentativePreference.reason: The confirmed-hit versus released-but-missed distinction is useful. I do not see enough evidence that the extra ring/pointer detail substantially improves pressure reading.

uncertainty: Only 22 sampled paired frames were inspected, not continuous video. Timing feel, tension, animation quality and normal-speed perceptual load remain inconclusive.
Three curated local windows support a narrow presentation comparison; neither all seed behavior nor whole-match readability was assessed.
Preparation tells do not establish cancellability, punish windows or tactical commitment rules. No gameplay changes occurred between alternatives.
No unique projectile lineage was reconstructed. Logs corroborate damage/empty AOE events but cannot establish visual pleasure.
reviews.overallVerdict: Tentatively prefer B for knowing a hit really happened. Its benefit to anticipation is modest in these samples, and reading initiative in four-way fights remains unresolved. Ready for a bounded owner comparison with those limits stated.

displaySummary.title: Hits are clearer; pressure is still hard to read
displaySummary.text: B helps separate a missed swing from a real hit. In the crowded fight I still have to trace shots to know who is pressuring whom, and the preparation detail is small. Slight preference for B, based on sampled stills rather than continuous viewing.

observations.fact: At 8.8 B adds a dark rim around blue’s preparation ring. At 9.3 B has a white crossed marker on red while both panels show red at 80 HP; the log records blue fireball damage at 9.25. At 9.7 red’s attack region is visible in both and no corresponding white damage marker is visible on blue; logs show red releasing melee at 9.633 with no subsequent damage there.
observations.interpretation: The victim marker gives a useful answer to “did that connect?” beyond existing particles. It helps distinguish red’s failed swipe from blue’s payoff. The preparation difference is subtle at this overview scale; I cannot claim it made anticipation easy in motion.

observations.fact: At 11.3 the fighters overlap closely and B adds a dark floor ring. The final sampled state holds red’s win at about 12.217; B retains a crossed hit marker at blue’s final position while blue is absent. Logs record red’s melee hits at 11.433 and 12.217.
observations.interpretation: A distinct payoff remains after the target disappears, which is helpful. Red closing on a fireball user creates understandable contrasting roles in both versions. The generic markers themselves do little to strengthen magical identity or make the outcome a richer surprise.

observations.fact: At 6.6 both have orange fireballs, pale blue circular magic and a bright yellow cast area. At 7.0 B adds a white crossed marker where green was eliminated, plus a dark launch ring near yellow’s spread. At 7.3 orange projectiles and pale blue remnants are still visible without a white marker on red. At 7.6 B shows a crossed marker on red while both show 91 HP. Logs locate green’s death at 6.983, yellow’s spread release at 6.883 and yellow’s two hits on red at 7.567/7.600. At 8.6 both still show separated orange projectiles and the red/yellow close exchange.
observations.interpretation: B clarifies the two local consequences without replacing recognizable ice/fire silhouettes. The spell continuing into a changed crowd is promising as a magical surprise, but these samples do not establish whether a viewer follows its ownership. Marker presence confirms damage, not the unique projectile responsible.

observations.fact: B adds dark preparation rims to multiple fighters at 0.1; at 0.7 it adds dark rings near green and yellow. At 1.3 red and green overlap with pale blue circles and a hit marker on red while yellow’s small orange volley is visible elsewhere. At 2.3 the large ice shard/circles and orange projectile train remain recognizable in both; B adds a marker near the red/green overlap. Logs show green’s spread damage around 0.983–1.017, yellow’s gatling release at 0.7 and red’s melee damage at 2.167.
observations.interpretation: The extra marks remain compact in these samples, but several outlines cluster around the same small bodies. This is the contrary case: the viewer may learn who was hit while still struggling to tell which magic caused it. More simultaneous symbols do not by themselves create a stronger character identity.

expectationAssessment.assessment: Tentative improvement in local consequence readability; enjoyment and animation quality remain inconclusive.
Inconclusive. Sampled stills and event timestamps cannot establish experienced buildup, tension or release.
Existing fire/ice/projectile pattern differences carry identity. B preserves them in inspected frames but generic rings/crosses add little new identity.
Inconclusive as experienced surprise. The logs support consequences from established abilities, but samples do not demonstrate recognition or emotional payoff.

Make public reporting explicit about which batch it represents; don't imply a 24-setup report with its current 16-setup configuration.

facts: Public report experiment and provenance both list seeds 1,7,19,42,101,211 and maxSeconds 120. There are 24 runs, 12 duel and 12 four-wizards, spanning two rotations.

observations.facts: At 9.1 a projectile sits between blue and red; at 9.3 red has lost 10 HP and B adds a white crossed hit mark. Log damage is blue fireball at 9.25. A has the same HP change and positions.
observations.interpretation: B makes actual damage a distinct visible event instead of requiring attention to the health display. This is a narrow cause/effect improvement.

observations.facts: The 9.7 frame has a pale melee swath but no damage after red release at 9.6333. At 11.3 B adds a dark-backed preparation ring around red. At 11.5 blue is at 12 HP after red melee at 11.4333. At held final 12.2167 B retains a white crossed marker where blue died; both alternatives show red wins.
observations.interpretation: A visible swing and a confirmed hit can be distinguished. The 11.3 cue is small and partly crowded by the two fighters; B is not a guarantee that a casual viewer can read every commitment.

observations.facts: At 6.7 yellow has a more visible dark-backed ring in B while green and red overlap. At 7.3 a falling ice effect is gone and small debris remains away from fighters; red still has 100 HP. At 7.6 red has 91 HP and B has a crossed hit mark by red. Logs show two yellow spread hits at 7.5667 and 7.6; the 7.3 ice debris did not correspond to damage.
observations.interpretation: The hit marker differentiates damage from harmless scenery effects, but does not identify which of the spread projectiles or which attacker caused it. I needed the logs for the latter claim.

observations.facts: B adds charge rings/pointers under green and yellow at 0.6; at 1.2 overlapping red and green carry several rings while yellow projectiles remain visible on the other side. At 2.4 the blue preparation ring/pointer shares space with the orange projectile stream.
observations.interpretation: The sparse procedural additions leave the larger four-way arrangement readable in these samples, but floor cues accumulate at close quarters. More cues do not resolve individual-shot attribution.

rankedConcerns.text: Confirmed-hit markers identify a damage location, not attacker, ability or projectile. Multiple spread hits at four19 7.6 remain causally ambiguous. Retain this contrary example and avoid claiming complete attribution.
Preparation circles and pointers are small at this arena scale and overlap in melee (duel 11.3; four1 1.2). These samples support added information, not guaranteed comprehension.
Stills and logs do not establish whether extra flashes improve experienced pacing or become distracting across a continuous fight. No animation-quality or entertainment rating is supported.

preference.reason: Separating confirmed damage from releases and harmless impacts is a useful information gain on identical gameplay. This does not establish a tactical, balance or owner-taste improvement.

uncertainty: Only sampled PNGs and logs inspected; no continuous clip viewing.
No unique cast/projectile lineage; attack-specific causation remains limited.
Selected examples and metadata cover a larger batch but do not establish readability for every seed.
WB-E001/E002 experienced enjoyment/pacing and WB-E005 pressure are inconclusive here; WB-E006 identity and WB-E007 surprise are only weakly addressed.
reviews.overallVerdict: Ready for a bounded owner comparison with a tentative B recommendation and visible attribution/overlap limits. The reported metadata blocker is corrected; no new blocker found.

displaySummary.title: Hits are easier to distinguish; their source can still be unclear
